messages:
Olivia: quick follow-up from the autoscaler RFC thread — sketching a 'slab' allocation primitive to decouple admission from pod orchestration. idea: a slab = fixed allocation unit (eg one GPU pod with X vram/slots). allocator requests slabs; pools advertise slab inventory. reduces churn and makes burst-credit accounting slab-native. thoughts?

Mateo: curious — how does slab differ from our current reservation object? is this purely naming or a runtime change?

Olivia: behaviorally different. reservations express tenant intent (throughput/slots). slabs are physical allocation quanta pool operators manage. reservations map to N slabs. by moving to slab leases we make admission coarser-grained and avoid frequent pod-level churn/flapping.

Jeremy: proto sketch for allocator<->pool handshake: 

```
requestAllocation(tenant_id, slab_count, slab_type_hint, priority_hint)
releaseAllocation(lease_id)
getPoolInventory() -> {available_slabs, warming_slabs, draining_slabs, slab_types}
```

admission response enum: GRANTED | QUEUED | DECLINED with optional estimated_wait_seconds and region_fallbacks.

Sasha: main concern: warmup time variability. large models need long kernel warmups and KV priming. slabs need explicit warm states so scheduler can reason about cold vs warm capacity. otherwise we hide latency costs.

Olivia: agreed. propose slab state machine: COLD -> WARMING -> WARM -> DRAINING. allocator uses WARM count for latency SLOs; it may accept cold slab with explicit tail-latency warning.

Anita: cost/packing angle: should slabs be homogeneous? big slabs waste capacity for small tenants; tiny slabs raise orchestration overhead. support slab types (small/med/large) so pool advertises a catalog and allocator matches tenant model profile.

Mateo: +1. pools publish slab_types metadata: e.g. small:1xA10-24G, med:1xA100-40G, large:1xA100-80G with per-type capacity counts. allocator picks best-fit type.

Jeremy: thinking about burst credits: today credits are numeric tokens; with slabs we can represent credits as slab-tokens. tenant has N burst-slabs/month; consuming a cold slab burns a slab-token. easier to reason about billing. we can back-compat translate fractional tokens during migration.

deploy-bot: PR opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/compare/slab-allocation-proto — draft adapter for existing pool operator.

Sasha: can we run historical sims? I'll run a 24h replay for top 50 tenants to measure percent-cold and p99 regressions if we adopt slab admission. need proto + sample workload.

Olivia: I'll drop a proto and small workload dump tonight. proposed rollout: 
- phase 0: add metric hooks + slab accounting in staging (no policy change)
- phase 1: soft opt-in: allocator can request slabs, but per-pod reservations still allowed
- phase 2: default slab admission; burst-slab billing enabled
- phase 3: tighten pool contracts, retire old reservation surface

Anita: any rough savings estimate for exec note? even a ballpark is useful.

Jeremy: back-of-envelope: fewer API calls to K8s and less node churn could save ~8-15% infra for mixed workloads; tail-heavy short-lived workloads might see 20-25%. sims will refine.

Mateo: happy to pair on adapter/proto next week.

Sasha: I'll own sim + eval harness. metrics to collect: percent_cold_served, p50/p95/p99 latency by tenant, lease_hold_time, slab_state_transitions.

Olivia: good. also an interface boundary note: allocator <-> pool should be minimal. pool doesn't need tenant semantics beyond slab_type and counts. allocator implements fairness/prioritization so Dedicated vs Private operators can implement pool side without tenant logic.

Jeremy: agree. keeping pool simple is important for adoption across Private/Dedicated.

Anita: one more product constraint — transferable slab leases across regions. allow tenant to accept regional fallback with an estimated egress_penalty_ms in admission. allocator makes cost/latency tradeoff.

Olivia: add region_preference field and optional egress_penalty_ms in admission response. allocator uses it in decision function.

Sasha: add telemetry tags: slab_type, slab_state, lease_age, warm_signal, region_hint. will help debugging SLO regressions.

Olivia: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with the proto, rollout plan, and a TODO for dashboards + sims. will post draft and pin link when ready. cc @Mateo @Jeremy @Anita.

infra-bot: noted. pinned thread will include RFC addendum link when published.
